# Field Notes: email activation

Prepared on 15 October 2026. **Email sending is not active.** The existing form still saves consented registrations privately in Firestore. No subscribers have been exported, contacted or added to another service. No new account, paid plan or Firebase billing change has been made.

## Information still needed from the owner

- Full name and email address approved for the public privacy notice. The private admin login is not publication permission.
- Existing email provider, or a free Brevo account with a verified sender.
- The public sign-up form URL generated by that account. Never paste an API key or account password into chat/source.

## Free route compatible with a static Spark-hosted website

Use a provider-hosted double-confirmation form. This avoids a client-side mail API key and a new server. Brevo documents a free allowance of 300 email sends per day; its form supports double confirmation and an optional final welcome email. Verify current account limits before activation.

In Brevo, create a Field Notes list and an email-only sign-up form with an unticked consent checkbox linking to `https://dainyelonthemove.com/privacy.html`. Select **Double confirmation**, then enable the final confirmation email. Use a verified sender and the text below. Preserve the provider's confirmation and unsubscribe links; do not substitute a homepage URL for a confirmation token. Disable optional open/click tracking where the account permits.

Sources: [form setup](https://help.brevo.com/hc/en-us/articles/208771869-Create-a-sign-up-form-in-Brevo), [free limits](https://help.brevo.com/hc/en-us/articles/208580669-FAQs-What-are-the-limits-of-the-Free-plan).

Dainyel

## Final connection and verification

1. Review the real published form URL, its double-confirmation setting, privacy/consent text and verified sender. A public URL is not proof that email sending is enabled.
2. Replace the new-signup route with the real form (a link works without JavaScript; an optional embedded form loads only after the visitor chooses it). Do not keep a second active Firestore signup alongside the provider flow.
3. Preserve the existing private Firestore records and owner access. Any migration needs a separate consent/provenance check; never silently mark these old registrations as confirmed or send a bulk email.
4. Update public signup/consent/privacy/cookie copy to describe the actual provider and an unsubscribe link. Add a direct provider-management link in the existing admin hub without exposing a secret.
5. Test only with the owner's authorised address: submit, receive the confirmation, confirm once, receive the welcome message, unsubscribe, retry/duplicate, mobile/keyboard and provider failure. The subscribed state must follow confirmation, not a mere HTTP success.
6. Deploy to staging, verify the real messages, then publish under the owner's approval for this correction. Do not claim email delivery works before an actual authorised inbox test.

## Retention operation

The revised privacy notice sets owner-managed retention: unpublished contributions up to 90 days; registrations up to 24 months or earlier withdrawal; privacy-request records up to 12 months after closure. Published contributions remain while relevant/consented and are reviewed annually. There is no automatic purge. Do not delete existing records or create an automation without explicit authority; make these manual reviews part of the owner workflow. Reconcile provider retention/consent records when activating delivery.
